title: brepocitinib
summary: Brepocitinib (PF-06700841) is a dual JAK1/TYK2 inhibitor discovered by Pfizer and further developed by Priovant Therapeutics. After initial development for several common immune-mediated diseases, Priovant shifted the program toward rare autoimmune disorders, including dermatomyositis. In the Ph. 3 VALOR trial, 30 mg QD brepocitinib significantly improved disease activity versus placebo. The results supported FDA approval of brepocitinib in August 2026 for adults with dermatomyositis, making it the first FDA-approved oral treatment specifically indicated for the disease.

title: DA-003
summary: DA-003 is a preclinical orthosteric MRGPRX2 antagonist developed by Deep Apple Therapeutics as a treatment for mast cell-driven immunological disorders. The molecule’s discovery story was presented at the ACS Fall 2026 First Time Disclosures session and is progressing toward clinical trials. Originating from an ultra-large-scale virtual screen and guided by computational modeling, the Deep Apple team delivered DA-003 as a potent MRGPRX2 antagonist with a favorable PK profile, dose-dependent in vivo inhibition of mast cell degranulation, and good tolerability in GLP toxicology studies.

Preclinically, VENT-03 demonstrates dose-dependent reductions of cGAMP levels and reductions in relevant inflammatory biomarkers, with a PK profile supporting once-daily dosing. title: ritonavir
summary: Ritonavir (Norvir®) is a protease inhibitor approved in March 1996 for the treatment of HIV-1 infection. Initially approved as a protease inhibitor, the compound’s role as a PK enhancer, increasing systemic longevity of other drugs through its inhibition of the drug-metabolizing enzyme CYP3A4, became a key utility for HIV-1 infection treatment. This PK-boosting ability was called to action again during the COVID-19 pandemic, gaining approval in combination with the SARS-CoV-2-targeting nirmatrelvir as Paxlovid®—making it a compound leveraged in global pandemics for two different diseases.

title: JNJ-2175
summary: JNJ-2175 is J&J’s ENPP3-targeting ADC, currently in Ph. 1 studies for advanced solid tumors. The program seeks to exploit the elevated, depolarized ENPP3 expression in tumors to enable selective payload delivery. summary: AZD3632 is an oral inhibitor of menin:KMT2A PPIs from Acerta Pharma/AstraZeneca disclosed at the First Time Disclosures sessions at the ACS Fall 2026 meeting in Chicago. title: enpatoran (M5049)
summary: Enpatoran (M5049) is a dual TLR7/8 antagonist currently in clinical development for lupus. Lupus erythematosus is a chronic heterogenous autoimmune disease characterized by production of pathogenic autoantibodies, with SLE accounting for ~70% of lupus cases, and can occur with or without skin-specific manifestations known as CLE. In the Ph. 2 WILLOW trial, enpatoran treatment led to significantly reduced disease severity in CLE patients, but not for SLE patients—motivating the initiation of the Ph. 3 ELOWEN trials for enpatoran’s potential regulatory registration in CLE.

title: diranersen
summary: AD is a neurodegenerative disease with symptoms of progressive loss of memory and cognitive function. An intriguing approach to treat AD involves tau level reduction via ASOs (antisense oligonucleotides). Biogen and Ionis Pharmaceuticals co-developed diranersen, which targets and silences the pre-mRNA from the MAPT gene that encodes tau. Diranersen reduced total tau levels, but the clinical trial missed its primary endpoint of demonstrating dose-dependency for cognitive decline. These results raise questions about the relationship between tau level reduction and clinical efficacy in AD.

title: TNG456
summary: Tango Therapeutics has advanced TNG456, its third oral, MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor, into clinical trials. Derived from the same oxamide scaffold as Tango’s earlier candidates TNG908 and vopimetostat (TNG462), TNG456 combines improved potency and selectivity for MTAP-deleted cells with good CNS exposure across preclinical species. The latter property is particularly notable because MTAP deletions occur in over 40% of high-grade malignant gliomas. Tango dosed the first patient in a Ph. 1/2 trial in May 2025 and published the molecule’s discovery story in May 2026.

summary: Golidocitinib (AZD4205/DZD4205) is an oral, selective JAK1 inhibitor discovered by AstraZeneca and developed by Dizal for oncology. The molecule applies JAK1-selective pathway inhibition to r/r PTCL, aiming to suppress JAK–STAT-driven lymphoma biology while avoiding cytopenias linked to JAK2 inhibition. After receiving FDA Fast Track designation, golidocitinib was conditionally approved in China for r/r PTCL in 2024 based on JACKPOT8 Part B, where it achieved a 44% ORR.

title: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236)
summary: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) is a non-covalent pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor from Revolution Medicines, which shows remarkable efficacy in tumors driven by RAS mutants that were previously considered “undruggable,” such as G12V/D/A/S, G13X, and Q61X. RMC-6236 exerts its action via a “tri-complex” mechanism, gluing RAS to the ubiquitously expressed chaperone protein, cyclophilin A.
